---
title: "Electrical resolution for lossless lines"
---

# Electrical resolution for lossless lines

`ElectricalResolution(max_frequency=10*u.GHz, sections_per_wavelength=40)` is
an immutable policy for a transmission line whose declared per-length R and G
matrices are exactly zero. It is exclusive with fixed `n_sections`. External
finite resistors and Ports remain ordinary circuit elements. The Plan stores
the policy, not a mesh; each resolved positive line length produces its own
integer section count before node allocation and stamping.

For reciprocal positive-definite L and C, factor L = A Aᵀ and diagonalize
B = Aᵀ C A. Its positive eigenvalues λ give modal delay per meter τ = √λ and
velocity v = 1/τ. With the slowest delay τmax, frequency fmax and M sections
per wavelength, hmax = 1/(M fmax τmax), N = max(1, ceil(length/hmax)), and
dx = length/N. The existing full conductor matrices are stamped in each Pi
section. Repeated modes are valid; no eigenvector labeling is required.

At real frequencies no higher than fmax, this defines a phase-increment bound
βm dx ≤ 2π/M. It is a *resolution convention*, not a bound on S-parameter,
root, or optimization error. Complex-frequency roots outside |ω|/(2π) ≤ fmax
are reported as outside the policy envelope; they are not automatically
remeshed or rejected. A different resolved length can cross an integer-N
boundary, so response derivatives with respect to position need not be smooth.

Both left and right physical lengths must remain strictly positive. Invalid
policy inputs, nonzero or missing R/G, non-positive modal eigenvalues, or a
non-finite or unrepresentable realization fail before numerical solution. The
fixed-count lossy line path is unchanged. This candidate does not add automatic
root search, topology scanning, accuracy certification, or a zero-length merge.
